Preview privacy

Your information.
Your choice.

How this unofficial concept works. This is a notice about the preview, not an approved privacy policy for Solomon Grinds.

What the preview does

The weekly planner keeps selections in the current page only. It does not create an account, save a booking or take payment. The enquiry form builds an email draft locally; it has no submission endpoint and sends nothing.

This website’s code adds no analytics, advertising trackers or browser cookies. Fonts and motion scripts are served with the site. The hosting service may process technical request information under its own policies; those practices need to be assessed before a live business launch.

When you choose an external link

Telephone, email, WhatsApp, mapping and existing payment links open the relevant external service. Their own terms and privacy practices apply. Information is shared with your chosen email app when you open a draft, and with Solomon if you then send it yourself.

Solomon’s live-site privacy notice needs updating

Visible correction: the existing notice refers to the Data Protection Acts 1988 and 2003 and promises an access-request response within 40 days. Current Data Protection Commission guidance uses GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, and says access requests must normally be answered without undue delay and within one month. A further two-month extension is possible in specified circumstances, with notice in the first month. Read DPC guidance ↗.

The current notice also lacks a completed cookie policy. This concept does not claim to repair the business’s actual data-handling practices. An owner-approved policy must cover the controller, purposes, legal bases, retention, recipients, safeguards and rights before launch.

Contact and rights

For information already shared with Solomon Grinds, use its published contact: caitrionahayes@yahoo.ie or 01 628 4171. For guidance on personal-data rights, visit the Data Protection Commission ↗.

Reviewed 11 October 2026. Sources: existing privacy statement ↗ and DPC Access and Portability guidance ↗.
